title: Orchestrated control-plane swap for hybrid fleet — checklist + Terraform notes
body:
Purpose:
This doc captures a pragmatic, rehearsal-friendly playbook for safely swapping the Kubernetes control plane in a mixed fleet (bare-metal + vSphere). Goal: allow us to move control-plane responsibilities (API, controllers, scheduler) off an at-risk control-plane pool to a replacement pool with minimal disruption and a clear rollback path.

Scope and assumptions:
- Target clusters: on-prem clusters that currently run a mixed control-plane topology (some control-plane VMs on vSphere, some static bare-metal masters).
- We assume HA k8s control plane (>=3 control-plane members recommended).
- Load-balancer in front of API (HAProxy/MetalLB/NSX) with ability to update backends via API or Terraform.
- Terraform is used to manage infrastructure objects: control-plane node instances, LB config, DNS records, and nodepool labels.
- kubeadm (or equivalent) based join/upgrade flows are used for control-plane node lifecycle.
- Telemetry: cluster-prometheus + node-exporter + control-plane logs flow to central observability.

High-level strategy:
1) Provision replacement control-plane pool (new flavor/quant/zone) alongside existing.
2) Do a full rehearsal on a staging cluster: dry-run all Terraform, apply, and perform API failover exercises.
3) Incrementally add new control-plane members; ensure etcd quorum maintained and etcd snapshot policy in place.
4) Switch LB backends to include new members while still keeping at least N old members online.
5) Remove old control-plane members one at a time, verifying scheduler + controller health and rolling back LB if needed.
6) Finalize by rebalancing taints/labels and updating Terraform state to new desired topology.

Pre-flight checklist (must pass before swap):
- Backup etcd snapshot created and uploaded to S3 (s3://redwood-etcd-backups/cluster-<name>/snap-YYYYMMDD).
- Prometheus alert rules for APIserver latency and controller-manager errors are silenced for the maintenance window (or monitored closely).
- All K8s CRs for critical operators (ingress, cert-manager, storage) have operator-managed leader-election verified.
- Terraform plan has been reviewed (PR linked) and state locked.
- On-call rotation and escalation contact list posted in the maintenance ticket.
- Rollback plan drafted and verified (see "Rollback checklist" section).

Quick commands (reference, adapt to env):
- Create etcd snapshot (kubeadm clusters): ETCDCTL_API=3 etcdctl --endpoints=https://127.0.0.1:2379 snapshot save /tmp/snap.db --cacert=/etc/kubernetes/pki/etcd/ca.crt --cert=/etc/kubernetes/pki/etcd/server.crt --key=/etc/kubernetes/pki/etcd/server.key
- Validate control-plane pod status: kubectl get pods -n kube-system -l component=kube-apiserver
- Check etcd health: etcdctl --endpoints=<peer-list> endpoint health --write-out=table
- Drain old control-plane node safely (control-plane nodes may host system pods): kubectl drain <node> --ignore-daemonsets --delete-emptydir-data --force

Terraform module notes (practical gotchas):
- Module: infra/controlplane_instance
  - Keep immutable tags for control-plane pools (eg. pool=v1-controlplane-2025-01) so we can trace ownership and avoid accidental drift.
  - Use lifecycle "create_before_destroy" carefully: for expensive bare-metal provisioning we cannot always create before destroy; gate with variable `allow_create_before_destroy`.
- Module: infra/loadbalancer_backend
  - Make LB targets an external list resource to allow staged updates: `lb_backend_pool = [old-members..., new-members...]`. We apply with `enable_new_members = false` initially.
  - Avoid direct DNS switch for low-level test; prefer toggling weight or enabling new backends with low weight, then increase weight.
- Module: cluster/taints_labels
  - Taint new control-plane nodes early (taint: dedicated=control-plane:NoSchedule) until they're fully validated.
- State management:
  - Lock state (remote S3+Dynamo/Cloud storage) before changes. If multiple TF ops are necessary (LB update then node create), split into separate plans and annotate PR with step IDs.

Step-by-step operational flow (detailed):
Preparation (T-72h to T-1h)
- T-72h: Create maintenance ticket (INF-2178). Add runbook link and assign SRE lead and platform engineer. Notify CS if customer clusters are affected.
- T-48h: Run terraform plan in a sandbox account for the cluster type; capture plan output.
- T-24h: Snapshot etcd, upload to backup storage, and verify restore test on a staging cluster.
- T-4h: Run canary deploy: provision 1 new control-plane member, join to cluster, validate status.

Planned swap window (T0)
1) Provision remaining new control-plane nodes via Terraform with `enable_new_members=true`. Wait for machines ready and kubelet registered.
2) On each new control-plane node: join to control plane (kubeadm join --control-plane ...) or ensure the bootstrap process completes. Validate pods: kube-apiserver, controller-manager, scheduler present and Running.
3) Verify etcd membership includes new nodes: `kubectl get endpoints -n kube-system` and `ETCDCTL` checks. Ensure quorum is >= majority.
4) Gradually add new nodes to LB backends: add with low weight (10%) and monitor error rates/latency for 10–15 minutes.
5) Increase weight in steps (10% -> 50% -> 100%) while keeping at least 2 old control-plane nodes registered.
6) After new nodes serving 100% and stable for 30min, start draining one old control-plane node at a time. After each drain, remove from LB, monitor workloads, and validate scheduler and control-plane metrics.
7) If anything degrades beyond thresholds (API errors >1% or control-plane restart rate high), immediate rollback to previous LB weights and re-add old nodes.

Rollback checklist:
- Re-add old control-plane node to LB with previous weight.
- Recreate any drained control-plane node (if unexpectedly deleted) from image/terraform or reprovision from cluster logs.
- Restore etcd from snapshot (last-resort). Document snapshot id and time.

Post-swap finalization:
- Update Terraform desired state to remove old pool resources. Run plan, review, and apply during a low-impact window.
- Annotate cluster metadata (tags/labels) to indicate new control-plane generation and date.
- Run smoke tests: schedule-job smoke (kube-system) and user-facing e2e tests.
- Re-enable alerts. Collect a 24h stabilization report and close maintenance ticket.

Troubleshooting heuristics (quick):
- APIServer high latency after adding new nodes: check kube-apiserver commandline for mis-configured cert SANs or incorrect etcd endpoints. Check kube-apiserver logs for failing webhook calls.
- Multiple control-plane pods CrashLoopBackOff: check volume mounts for kube-apiserver (pem files), check /etc/hosts and DNS resolution between nodes.
- Etcd member not joining: verify firewall between peers (2379/2380), verify certs and correct initial cluster string.

Open questions / TODOs:
- Decide canonical approach for LB weight adjustments vs DNS TTL swap. Preference: LB weight transitions for faster rollback; document exceptions where DNS swap is required (eg. NSX-only customers).
- Validate integration with vSphere anti-affinity rules for control-plane VMs. Need a small terraform test to ensure vSphere placement doesn't violate quorum. (PR: infra/vsphere-anti-affinity-test pending)
- Add automated pre-flight checks into the cluster CLI: `rwi cluster validate-controlplane-swap --cluster foo` to reduce human checklist steps.

Runbook rehearsal notes (staging playthrough 2025-01-29):
- Rehearsal result: new control-plane nodes added successfully. Observed transient spike in API latency for ~90s during LB weight bump from 50%->100%. No pod evictions observed.
- Lessons: increase LB weight ramp window to 5m between steps; ensure controller-manager has adequate CPU during join.

Safety and sign-off:
- Required approvers before production swap: SRE lead (Diego), Platform eng (Maya), Security (Priya).
- If cluster is customer-managed in a private VPC, notify customer ops at least 48h in advance and provide an estimated maintenance window.

Appendix: useful links and references:
- Staging rehearsal notes: Confluence: /display/INF/Hybrid+Control+Plane+Rehearsals
- GitHub infra PR for Terraform changes: https://github.com/redwood-inference/infra/pull/488
- JIRA maintenance ticket: INF-2178

Notes to self: keep this doc lightweight, convert to a shorter checklist for on-call runbook, and add automated verification steps (k8s probe that asserts X new control-plane members present).

Unresolved: where to place the canonical boolean toggle `enable_create_before_destroy` in modules for mixed fleets; long-term aim: have a module param mapping by provider (vSphere -> allow CBD true, bare-metal -> false) and guard in CI tests.
